validated_work_order.understanding: useSchedules (packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useSchedules.ts:135-190) tears the account register for one query round trip every time the schedules table changes. The schedules liveQuery's onData fires again on any change to the schedules table. It unsubscribes the two dependent queries, then declares `let statuses: ScheduleStatuses = new Map()` and `let postedTransactionsBySchedule = new Map()`, reopens both queries, and calls publish() from whichever returns first. The posted-transactions query is a plain $or over three columns; the status query is an $or of per-schedule $and branches with a calculate upstream, so the cheap query is expected to win and the tear is the common case. Publishing a fresh schedule list against an empty status map makes every schedule fail isForPreview (statuses.get returns undefined, which is not in ['due','upcoming','missed','paid'] — packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts:498-507), so computeSchedulePreviewTransactions returns [], and usePreviewTransactions clears previewTransactions. The register blanks and then repopulates. setIsLoading(true) sits in the effect body keyed on [query, upcomingLength] and never in onData, so only the initial mount is masked; a refresh is not, and Balance.tsx:92-95 gates only on isLoading. I reproduced this: driving the hook through two onData cycles with the posted-transactions query resolving first leaves result.current.statuses.size === 0 while result.current.schedules.length === 2. The fix the epic names is to seed the two locals from the currently published data before reopening the queries. One correction to the epic: seeding alone does NOT stop statusLabels being rebuilt on every posted-transaction event — publish() constructs a new Map unconditionally (useSchedules.ts:161-166), so a fresh Map identity is produced on each publish even when statuses is unchanged by identity. Verified with a failing identity assertion; reusing the previous statusLabels when the statuses Map is unchanged by identity makes it pass, and is a separate two-line change in the same publish body. This revision addresses the one objection raised against v1, which was entirely about how QA drives the browser criteria, not about the fix: v1 told the tester to trigger the refresh from Schedules > the schedule > Edit and then watch the register. That is unobservable, because /schedules and /accounts/:id are sibling <Route> elements under one <Routes> (FinancesApp.tsx:254, :275, :403), so opening the Schedules page unmounts Account and with it the SchedulesProvider at components/accounts/Account.tsx:2115. Returning remounts a provider whose data is the empty initial state with isLoading true (useSchedules.ts:96-103), so the rows are absent on arrival because the provider just started, not because of the bug. The criteria below drive the edit from inside the register itself.
validated_work_order.root_cause: The schedules liveQuery's onData reinitialises both dependent Maps to empty on every refresh and publishes from whichever dependent query returns first, so the cheaper posted-transactions query publishes a fresh schedule list against an empty status map. isForPreview then rejects every schedule and the register empties for a round trip. setIsLoading(true) lives in the effect body only, so nothing masks a refresh.
validated_work_order.approach: Seed the two per-refresh locals from the last published ScheduleData instead of from empty Maps, held in a ref so onData (which closes over a stale render's `data`) reads the current value. Three edits, all inside useSchedules.ts: (1) add `const latestDataRef = useRef<ScheduleData>(data);` beside the three existing LiveQuery refs; (2) in the schedules onData, replace the two empty-Map declarations with reads of latestDataRef.current.statuses and latestDataRef.current.postedTransactionsBySchedule, and update the existing comment above them, which currently explains the reset and would otherwise describe behaviour the code no longer has; (3) in publish(), build the next ScheduleData object, reuse latestDataRef.current.statusLabels when `statuses === previous.statuses` by identity, otherwise build it as today, then assign latestDataRef.current = next before setData(next). Everything else in the hook is unchanged — the same queries are opened, the same teardown runs, isLoading is untouched. The seed is deliberately NOT filtered to the incoming schedule ids: a schedule added by the edit has no seeded status and is therefore excluded for one round trip, which is correct and is the conservative direction, whereas seeding a stale status onto a newly completed schedule is harmless because isForPreview also tests `!schedule.completed` against the fresh schedule object. Two files plus a release note. No component, query builder, or consumer changes.

files.change: Add `const latestDataRef = useRef<ScheduleData>(data);` after the postedQueryRef declaration (line 108). In the schedules liveQuery's onData, replace `let statuses: ScheduleStatuses = new Map();` and `let postedTransactionsBySchedule = new Map<string, PostedScheduleTransaction[]>();` (lines 147-151) with reads seeded from latestDataRef.current, and rewrite the comment block immediately above them (lines 143-146) so it explains that both queries start from the last published values rather than from empty. In publish(), stop calling setData with an inline object literal: read `const previous = latestDataRef.current`, set `const statusLabels = statuses === previous.statuses ? previous.statusLabels : new Map([...statuses.keys()].map(key => [key, getStatusLabel(statuses.get(key) || '')]))`, build `const next: ScheduleData = { schedules, statuses, statusLabels, postedTransactionsBySchedule }`, then assign `latestDataRef.current = next;` before `setData(next);`. Leave the isUnmounted guard, the teardown of the two dependent queries, the error handling, setIsLoading, and the return shape untouched.
files.why: Root cause. The ref rather than the `data` state variable is required because onData is created inside the effect, which only re-runs on [query, upcomingLength], so it closes over a stale `data` — reading state directly would seed from the initial empty Maps on every refresh and change nothing.

files.change: Add tests covering the refresh seed. Reuse the existing `calls` array harness: calls[0] is the schedules query, and each schedules onData pushes the status query then the posted-transactions query, so the first cycle is calls[1]/calls[2] and the second is calls[3]/calls[4]. IMPORTANT: hoist the query into a `const query = q('schedules').select('*')` outside the renderHook callback in any new test that asserts on isLoading or on publish output — the existing tests build the query inline (lines 51, 74, 94), which yields a fresh object per render, re-runs the effect, and leaves isLoading stuck at true. Use next_date values relative to `monthUtils.currentDay()` (import * as monthUtils from '@actual-app/core/shared/months') rather than fixed dates.
files.why: The behaviour is a race between two mocked queries, which this harness drives deterministically; without a test the seed can be reverted silently, because the existing suite still passes with the reset in place.

files.change:
Create a release note with frontmatter `---
category: Bugfix
authors: [Shivam-Fl]
---` followed by one sentence: 'Fix the Upcoming rows in an account register briefly disappearing when a schedule is edited or synced.'
files.why: upcoming-release-notes/ is this repo's convention for user-visible fixes and every comparable AI-authored fix in that directory ships one.

cases: keeps the published statuses when the posted-transactions query wins the race on refresh: first cycle, deliver schedules then status then posted and assert statuses.size is 2; second schedules onData, deliver ONLY the posted query (calls[4]) and assert schedules.length is 2 AND statuses.size is 2 — the regression test, failing with 0 on the unmodified hook

reuses the same statusLabels Map instance when statuses is unchanged by identity: capture result.current.statusLabels before the refresh, deliver only the posted query, assert it is toBe the captured value
rebuilds statusLabels once the status query delivers a new map: after the refresh, deliver calls[3] and assert the statusLabels instance is no longer the captured one

does not seed a status for a schedule added by the refresh: after a refresh whose schedule list includes a new id, delivering only the posted query leaves statuses.has(newId) false, and delivering the status query then makes it true
still unsubscribes the previous status and posted queries when schedules refresh, and still unsubscribes every query on unmount (the two existing tests, unchanged)

no change required — the existing suite must keep passing untouched; it mocks useCachedSchedules wholesale and does not exercise the hook's refresh path, which is why the regression was invisible to it

acceptance.check: With Upcoming rows showing in an account register, editing one of those schedules from inside the register leaves the rows continuously on screen — they never blank out and reappear
acceptance.how_to_verify: Open the demo budget (Welcome > 'Try the demo'), go to the Bank of America register at /accounts/<id>, confirm Upcoming rows for 'Phone bills', 'Internet bill' and 'Utilities'. Each Upcoming row carries a schedule button in its payee cell — data-testid="schedule-icon" (TransactionsTable.tsx:938-947), rendered for preview rows too because they carry a schedule id. Click it: the schedule editor opens as a MODAL over the still-mounted register (TransactionList.tsx:334-343 dispatches pushModal; <Modals /> renders at App.tsx:239-241 as a sibling of <AppInner />, which owns the Routes). Change the Amount, Save, watch the rows. STAY ON /accounts/<id> — do NOT navigate to the Schedules page and back; that unmounts the Account route and its SchedulesProvider, so you would be judging a fresh mount, not the refresh. Rows must never be absent between save and settle. The bug is a one-round-trip tear, so it may be a single dropped frame: repeat the cycle several times or throttle the network with Playwright/CDP network conditions. Equivalent trigger: right-click the row > 'View Schedule' (useTransactionRowContextActions.ts:137-155) — same modal, same page.

acceptance.check: The register renders its Upcoming rows from the currently published schedule data, without waiting for the slower status query to return
acceptance.how_to_verify: Same setup and same in-register procedure as AC-1: stay on /accounts/<id>, click the data-testid="schedule-icon" button on an Upcoming row, change the amount, Save, observe the rows without navigating away. Edit a schedule whose status does not change (an amount-only edit). After the fix the rows are already on screen and correct the moment the schedules query fires, computed from the previously published status map, so nothing visible changes at the save and nothing changes when the status query lands afterwards — the row set and their ordering stay identical throughout. On the unfixed hook the row set empties for one round trip at the save instead.

acceptance.check: A test drives useSchedules through two onData cycles with the posted-transactions query resolving first, and the published data never pairs a schedule list with an empty status map
acceptance.how_to_verify: Run `yarn workspace @actual-app/web run test src/hooks/useSchedules.test.ts`. The named case is 'keeps the published statuses when the posted-transactions query wins the race on refresh'. It must be shown to fail on the unmodified hook (statuses.size === 0) and pass with the change. This is the authoritative proof for the ticket: the race is two local queries landing in a particular order, which a browser cannot be made to produce on demand.

acceptance.check: The existing useSchedules and usePreviewTransactions tests still pass, and statusLabels keeps its identity across a refresh that does not change statuses
acceptance.how_to_verify: Run `yarn workspace @actual-app/web run test src/hooks/useSchedules.test.ts src/hooks/usePreviewTransactions.test.ts` — all pre-existing cases pass. The statusLabels identity case is 'reuses the same statusLabels Map instance when statuses is unchanged by identity'.

acceptance.check: A schedule completed from the register's row context menu leaves the register promptly rather than lingering on a stale status, and a schedule added afterwards gets its row once its status is known
acceptance.how_to_verify: Two halves, judged differently — read both. (1) COMPLETED, judged for promptness, entirely inside the register: stay on /accounts/<id>. Right-click the 'Internet bill' Upcoming row — a one-time (non-recurring) schedule in the demo budget (packages/loot-core/src/mocks/budget.ts:977-1000), so 'Mark as completed' is visible rather than hidden (useTransactionRowContextActions.ts:110-118 hides it for recurring schedules) — and choose it. That dispatches schedule/update with completed: true (Account.tsx:1578-1590), touching the schedules table and triggering a refresh in place. The row must disappear at once, not one round trip later. (2) ADDED, judged for presence only, never for continuity: a new schedule can only be created from the Schedules page ('New schedule' dispatches schedule-edit with empty options, components/schedules/index.tsx:38), so navigate to Schedules, create a schedule dated inside the upcoming window, save, then navigate BACK to the Bank of America register. Judge this half as: once the register has finished its initial load, the new schedule's row is present. Do not judge continuity on this half and do not count the mount-time blank on arrival as a failure — the provider starts empty on every mount (useSchedules.ts:96-103), out of scope for this ticket.

qa_script: Boot with `yarn start` and open http://localhost:3001; the pipeline env is compose mode, base_url http://localhost:3001, no login (qa_auth.mode is none).

On the Welcome screen choose 'Try the demo' — the demo budget is created with real schedules on Bank of America ('Phone bills' monthly, 'Internet bill' one-time, 'Utilities' monthly; packages/loot-core/src/mocks/budget.ts:944+), so Upcoming rows are present without hand-building data.
Open the Bank of America account and confirm the Upcoming rows are listed. This page must stay mounted for steps 4-7 — do not navigate to /schedules and back in the middle of an observation.

Trigger a schedules-table refresh from inside the register: click the schedule button on an Upcoming row (data-testid="schedule-icon", aria-label 'See schedule details'), which opens the schedule editor as a modal OVER the register rather than navigating; change the Amount; Save; and watch the rows. They must not blank. Never navigate away between opening the editor and observing the rows.

For a visible tear, repeat the open-edit-save cycle several times, or throttle the network with Playwright/CDP network conditions — the bug is a single query round trip and is easy to miss at full speed.
Repeat with the context-menu trigger instead (right-click the row > 'View Schedule') to confirm the path is not specific to the icon button.

Complete a schedule from the row context menu: right-click the 'Internet bill' Upcoming row (one-time, so 'Mark as completed' is not hidden) and confirm its row leaves the register promptly rather than after a delay.

For the added-schedule half only, go to Schedules, create a schedule dated inside the upcoming window, save, return to the account, and confirm the new row is present once the register has finished loading. Do not judge continuity on this step — it necessarily involves a remount.
Watch the browser console throughout; a `Cannot read properties of undefined` from the schedules path would indicate the seed published a schedule list with no matching statuses.
risks: The seed is stale by design for one round trip: between the schedules query firing and the status query returning, the register renders rows computed from the PREVIOUS status map. If a schedule's status genuinely changed in the edit, the row can show its old status briefly before correcting — strictly better than the current behaviour, which shows nothing at all for the same window. AC-5 pins the two edges that matter.

A schedule ADDED by the refresh has no seeded status and is excluded from the register for one round trip, because isForPreview treats an unknown status as not-for-preview. Conservative direction, but a newly created schedule's first row can appear a beat after the save.

The statusLabels identity reuse keys on Map identity. Any future code that MUTATES the statuses Map in place instead of replacing it would leave statusLabels stale; the current code always builds a fresh Map per status-query delivery, so the invariant holds today, but it is an invariant the next editor must know about.

The browser criteria are judged on a path QA must not leave (/accounts/<id>). If QA drives the edit from the Schedules page and navigates back, every browser criterion is measured across a remount and will report a false failure. This is why the procedure is spelled out in AC-1, AC-2, AC-5 and qa_script rather than stated once.

No forbidden path is touched: the change is confined to packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useSchedules.ts, its test, and a new file under upcoming-release-notes/. Nothing under .sdlc/**, .github/**, or the approved docs is modified.
No new host is contacted by this change. The existing api_allowlist (localhost, 127.0.0.1, api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com) already covers the app's runtime traffic, and nothing is added.
out_of_scope: Moving setIsLoading(true) into onData so a refresh is masked by the loading state — the seed makes the gap disappear without touching isLoading, and flipping isLoading on refresh would blank the register for the round trip it is meant to hide.
A loading state in the register UI. There is none today and none is added; AC-1 is about continuity, not about a spinner.

The blank rows on a fresh mount of the register (the empty initial ScheduleData at useSchedules.ts:96-103). That is what AC-5's added-schedule half is explicitly not judged on, and it is a separate behaviour from the refresh tear this ticket fixes.
Widening the change to usePreviewTransactions.ts, Balance.tsx, or the schedule query builders. They consume the hook correctly; the defect is entirely in what the hook publishes.
Deduplicating or cancelling in-flight dependent queries across a refresh, or any change to the tear-down ordering that the existing unsubscribe tests already cover.

Making the two dependent queries atomic (publish only once both have delivered). The comment in the hook explains why this is deliberately not done: it strands the register in its loading state whenever one query is slow. IAC-2 depends on the current independent-publish behaviour.
Scheduling or sync-side changes. Nothing about how schedule edits propagate is touched.

Fixing the inline-`q('schedules')`-per-render construction in the three pre-existing useSchedules tests. It is a latent test-hygiene flaw (re-runs the effect, pins isLoading true), it does not make those tests wrong, and correcting it is its own change; the new tests hoisting the query is what matters here.
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: The failure is reproduced deterministically in the unit harness, the fix is trialled in a copy of the hook against both the reproduction and the existing suite, and the two edge cases the seed could plausibly break were tested rather than reasoned about. The rejection of v1 concerned the browser procedure only; I re-verified every claim it made against the code before rewriting — the sibling-route unmount (FinancesApp.tsx:254/275/403), the provider at Account.tsx:2115, the modal dispatch at TransactionList.tsx:334-343, the schedule-icon button at TransactionsTable.tsx:938-947 rendering for preview rows, the context menu at useTransactionRowContextActions.ts:137-186, <Modals /> as a sibling of <AppInner /> at App.tsx:236-241, and that schedule creation is reachable only from the Schedules page (components/schedules/index.tsx:38), which is why AC-5's two halves are judged differently. The residual uncertainty is behavioural, not technical: how visible a one-round-trip tear is in a browser.
evidence: Reproduced the tear in a vitest harness against the unmodified hook: renderHook(useSchedules), deliver schedules -> status -> posted, assert statuses.size === 2 (passes), then fire a second schedules onData and deliver ONLY the posted query (calls[4]); result.current.schedules.length === 2 but result.current.statuses.size === 0, and the assertion `statuses.size > 0` failed with 'expected 0 to be greater than 0'.

Confirmed the epic's secondary claim does not hold on its own: with seeding applied but statusLabels still built unconditionally in publish (useSchedules.ts:161-166), asserting result.current.statusLabels is the same object before and after the refresh FAILED. Adding the identity reuse made it pass.

Verified the candidate fix: seeding both maps from a latestDataRef plus the statusLabels identity reuse keeps statuses.size at 2 across the refresh, and the existing six useSchedules tests all pass against it.

Verified the edge cases against the candidate fix: a schedule added by the refresh has no seeded status and is excluded until the status query delivers, then appears; a schedule marked completed by the refresh still leaves the register immediately because isForPreview tests the fresh schedule object's own `completed` flag (schedules.ts:503-506).

Confirmed the v1 rejection's mechanism in code: /schedules and /accounts/:id are sibling routes under one <Routes> (FinancesApp.tsx:254, 275, 403), Account mounts SchedulesProvider at Account.tsx:2115, and a returning mount starts from the empty initial ScheduleData with isLoading true (useSchedules.ts:96-103) — so a refresh observed across a navigation is indistinguishable from a fresh mount.

Confirmed the in-register triggers QA will use: the schedule icon button (data-testid="schedule-icon", TransactionsTable.tsx:938-947) is rendered inside PayeeIcons, which both payee cells (TransactionsTable.tsx:718, :814) render for every row including previews; preview rows carry a schedule id (usePreviewTransactions.ts:122,132). Both it and 'View Schedule' dispatch pushModal schedule-edit, and <Modals /> sits outside the Routes subtree, so the register stays mounted with the modal over it.

Confirmed AC-5's completed half is reachable in the demo budget: 'Mark as completed' is hidden only for recurring schedules (useTransactionRowContextActions.ts:110-118) and dispatches schedule/update {completed:true} (Account.tsx:1578-1590); the demo budget's 'Internet bill' is a one-time schedule (budget.ts:977-1000) and so is completable.

Confirmed AC-5's added half can only be driven from the Schedules page: `schedule-edit` with empty options — the only `adding` branch — is dispatched solely from components/schedules/index.tsx:38. Hence that half is specified as presence-after-load rather than continuity.

A first run of the reproduction appeared to show isLoading stuck true; that was an artefact of building the query inline so the effect re-ran each render, not the hook's behaviour — real callers memoise the query (Account.tsx:2091, the mobile pages).

All scratch files (__repro.test.ts, __trial*.test.ts, useSchedulesTrial*.ts) were deleted; `git status` shows only the untracked plan/ directory plus work-order.json, and `git diff` against HEAD is empty.

alternatives_considered.approach: Set isLoading true in onData so the refresh is masked by the loading state, as the initial mount already is
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That blanks the register for exactly the round trip it is meant to hide: usePreviewTransactions returns [] while isSchedulesLoading is true, and Balance.tsx returns null on isLoading. It converts a data tear into a loading flicker and would break AC-1 rather than fix it.

alternatives_considered.approach: Have QA drive the edit from the Schedules page and navigate back to judge continuity
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This is what v1 specified and it is unobservable: navigating away unmounts the Account route and its SchedulesProvider, so what QA would watch is a fresh provider's initial load. It was the sole reason v1 was rejected, and it is why every browser criterion here names the in-register modal procedure instead.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add an e2e/Playwright case that opens the schedule modal over the register and asserts on row continuity, so the browser criterion is enforced by CI rather than by QA procedure
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The tear is one local query round trip; a Playwright assertion would race the very event it is trying to observe and be flaky in exactly the way this ticket is about. The deterministic proof is the unit test in AC-3, and the browser criteria are written to be judged on row continuity rather than on catching a single frame.

alternatives_considered.approach: Hold the previous status map in a ref but publish only once both dependent queries have delivered in the current cycle
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This is the atomic-publish approach the existing comment at useSchedules.ts:143-146 already rejects: the two queries are independent subscriptions and one can be arbitrarily slow, so the register would sit in its loading state until the slower one lands. IAC-2 explicitly requires the register to render without waiting for the slower query.

alternatives_considered.approach: Seed only the statuses map and leave postedTransactionsBySchedule empty on refresh
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Both locals are published from the same body and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions consumes both; seeding one and resetting the other produces a mixed state (correct statuses, empty occurrence index) that would re-show occurrences the user had already posted. I trialled seeding both and verified the added/completed edge cases hold.

alternatives_considered.approach: Derive statusLabels with useMemo over statuses instead of an explicit identity check in publish
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: statusLabels is built inside publish, which runs from a query callback rather than during render, so a useMemo keyed on statuses would not decide the value. It also does not address the case where statuses is unchanged — the map is rebuilt on every publish regardless. The identity check inside publish is the direct expression of the invariant.

assumptions: The three existing useSchedules tests that build `q('schedules').select('*')` inline inside renderHook are not themselves broken; the fresh-per-render query re-runs the effect, but those tests never assert isLoading and their assertions still hold. The new tests must hoist the query.
getStatus reads `monthUtils.currentDay()`, so any test asserting a specific status string must use dates relative to today rather than fixed literals.

The demo budget created by 'Try the demo' contains three Bank of America schedules — 'Phone bills' (monthly), 'Internet bill' (one-time, dated yesterday) and 'Utilities' (monthly) — so AC-1, AC-2 and AC-5 are reachable without hand-built data, and 'Internet bill' is the one whose row context menu offers 'Mark as completed'.

QA can drive the app at http://localhost:3001 with no login (compose mode, qa_auth.mode none) and can reach a row's context menu by right-clicking it, as the schedule actions menu is registered per row via useContextMenu.

No consumer depends on the status map being empty immediately after a refresh. usePreviewTransactions, Balance.tsx, RuleEditor.tsx and useCategoryScheduleGoalTemplates all treat statuses as a lookup keyed by schedule id, so a map carrying one round trip of stale values is well-formed for every one of them.
unknowns: Whether the tear is perceptible at full speed in a browser. It is a single query round trip and may be one dropped frame; the qa_script therefore calls for repeated edits or network throttling rather than a single observation. If QA cannot make it visible at all, AC-3's test is the authoritative proof and AC-1 should be judged on the rows being continuously correct rather than on catching the flicker.

Whether other consumers of useCachedSchedules render anything user-visible from statuses during the refresh window that would now show a stale value where it previously showed nothing. RuleEditor.tsx:397 and useCategoryScheduleGoalTemplates.ts read statusLabels by schedule id; neither was traced far enough to rule out a stale label being visible for a round trip.
validated_work_order.debate_summary: Single-stage plan (no council), so no critique/arbiter exchange. v1 was rejected on a single objection, entirely about how QA was told to drive the browser criteria rather than about the fix: it told the tester to open Schedules > the schedule > Edit and then watch the register rows, which unmounts the Account route and its SchedulesProvider first, so every browser criterion would have been judged across a remount instead of the refresh — and AC-1's own text contradicted itself by asking the tester to watch register rows from a page that does not render a register. This revision answers it by moving the trigger inside the register: the Upcoming row's own data-testid="schedule-icon" button and the row context menu's 'View Schedule' both dispatch the schedule-edit modal, which renders outside the Routes subtree, so the register stays mounted and the liveQuery re-fires in place. AC-1, AC-2, AC-5 and qa_script steps 4-7 all name that procedure and instruct QA explicitly not to navigate away. AC-5's completed half uses the row context menu's 'Mark as completed' as the objection required — which also turned out to be the only way to reach it in the demo budget, since that item is hidden for recurring schedules and only 'Internet bill' is one-time. AC-5's added half necessarily involves leaving the page (a new schedule can only be created from the Schedules page), so it is specified as presence-after-load and explicitly not judged for continuity. AC-3 and AC-4 are unchanged, as the objection said. The substantive technical finding is unchanged from v1 and is a correction to the epic's stated fix: seeding alone does not stop statusLabels being rebuilt on every publish, verified with a failing identity assertion, so the identity reuse is specified as a separate required change in the same publish body.
residual_risks: QA cannot drive the exact race in a live browser — it is two local queries landing in a particular order — so AC-1 and AC-2 are judged on continuity of the rows rather than on observing the tear directly. AC-3 is the deterministic proof and is the one to trust if the browser observation is ambiguous.

The browser criteria now carry an instruction QA must follow (stay on /accounts/<id>). A QA run that ignores it and judges continuity across a navigation will report a false failure against a correct implementation; the procedure is repeated in four places to make that unlikely, and the false-failure mode is stated in AC-5's text as well as in risks[].
The refresh path has no e2e coverage upstream; this change adds unit coverage only. A regression that only shows up with a real sync event landing mid-refresh would not be caught by the added tests.

route_request.reason: Not requested for this ticket's work — raised only so a human can decide whether the stale-status window (up to one query round trip showing a previous status after an edit that changes it) is acceptable as a user-visible trade, or whether the epic should be re-split to require an atomic publish with a real loading state instead. The fix as specified is correct and tested, and v1's sole rejection concerned QA procedure rather than this trade; the question is product tolerance for briefly-stale status text, which a planner should not settle alone.
